disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Alaska seasons are set by Game Management Unit (GMU); zones below use GMUs, which the app cannot resolve to a map pin — always verify the current GMU boundaries, emergency-order closures, and regulations with ADF&G before trapping. Local regulations, ordinances, and state park rules may prohibit trapping.

license_summary.trapping_license: An Alaska trapping license is required to take furbearers. Consult ADF&G for license types, fees, and sealing-officer locations.
license_summary.sealing: Beaver, fisher, lynx, marten (in listed units), river otter, wolf, and wolverine must be sealed within 30 days after the close of the season. Mountain lions must be sealed on or before the 10th day after removal from the trap (skull and hide, evidence of sex attached, both unfrozen). Unit 2 wolves: call the ADF&G Ketchikan office within 7 days of take and seal hides within 15 days.
license_summary.emergency_orders: Lynx seasons in Units 7, 14C, 15 and Units 11, 13, 14A, 14B, 16 may be closed by emergency order and are reviewed annually — check ADF&G emergency orders before trapping lynx.
license_summary.closed_areas: Numerous areas are closed to trapping (Juneau-area strips/trails/refuges, Chugach State Park species closures, JBER, Kenai Moose Research Center, McNeil River Sanctuary, Unit 20B Creamer's Field registration, and others). See the booklet's 'Areas Closed to Trapping' and 'Additional Restrictions' for each section — not enumerated here.

sources.title: 2026–27 Alaska Trapping Regulations (ADF&G booklet, effective July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027)
sources.notes: All season tables, limits, sealing requirements, and area closures read directly from this booklet. Archived locally in hidden_files/season-research/alaska/.

verification.confirmation_notes: The 2026–27 ADF&G trapping booklet (2026-07-01–2027-06-30 regulatory year) verified 2026-09-18. All season dates and limits read from the five regional sections (Southeast Units 1-5; Southcentral Units 6-8, 14C, 15; Central/Southwest Units 9-11, 13, 14A, 14B, 16, 17; Interior Units 12, 19-21, 24, 25, 26B, 26C; Western/Arctic Units 18, 22, 23, 26A). Fisher and mountain lion appear only in the Southeast section.
known_gaps: GMU zones are descriptive — the app cannot resolve GMU boundaries; unit-subunit boundary descriptions (e.g., the Unit 4 Chichagof Island line) are not modeled as polygons.
Areas closed to trapping are summarized, not enumerated — users must check the booklet's 'Areas Closed to Trapping' and 'Additional Restrictions' for their unit.
Scientific names are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in the ADF&G trapping regulations — all flagged scientific_name_verified=false; weasel is null because the booklet groups species.
All entries use America/Anchorage; the western Aleutians (Unit 10) observe Hawaii-Aleutian Time — a one-hour difference the app should account for.
No red fox season is listed for Units 6, 7, 8, 14C, 15; no coyote or wolf season for Unit 8 (Kodiak) — noted, not modeled as closed entries.
Lynx seasons may be closed by emergency order — the app should direct users to check ADF&G emergency orders.

Detailed method rules (beaver house/den protection, aircraft same-day-shooting rules, wolf steel-trap/snare diameter restrictions, Unit 26A aircraft restrictions) are noted per season, not fully modeled.
